key_insight: Scale-induced averaging attenuates variability in panel ultimate load, while spatially correlated interface weak spots remain critical to predicting early damage initiation and location.
engineering_relevance: Match uncertainty-model complexity to the design criterion: spatially uniform variability for global load capacity and correlated random fields for local skin–stringer bond integrity.
method: Extend likelihood-free Bayesian calibration from Mode I to Mode II using experimental coupon data.
Propagate interface variability from coupons to aerospace panels through simulation-based stochastic finite elements.
Compare B-basis design values, spatially uniform variability, and spatially correlated random fields.
evidence_signal: Coupon experiments inform interface calibration, and panel simulations show uncertainty attenuation in ultimate load but sensitivity of early damage to local weak spots.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation metrics; transferring coupon-calibrated spatial variability to industrial panels needs careful verification.
paper_title: Scaling of Interface Variability in Aerospace Composite Structures: A Multi-scale Stochastic Approach from Local Identification to Panel Response
